question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom Phrase.

To be on one's last legs
solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"To be on one's last legs"** means to be very near to death or in a very weakened or poor condition. (मृत्यु के निकट होना)

 
 
• **Example: **The old dog is on** its last legs**; it can barely move now.
 
 
 
• **"To be near death"** refers to a situation where someone is about to die or is in a very poor state of health. (मृत्यु के निकट होना)
 
 
• **Example: **The patient was so ill that he was **on his last legs.**
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of the idiom **'To be on one's last legs'** is **'To be near death'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To fuss about a trifle** (तुच्छ बात पर हो-हल्ला मचाना): To make a big deal out of something insignificant.

 
 
• **Example:** She always** fusses about trifles**, like when the towels aren't perfectly aligned.
 
 
 
• **To get married soon** (जल्द ही शादी करना): To be on the verge of getting married.
 
 
• **Example: **They've been engaged for a year and are** getting married soon.**
 
 
 
• **Last day of work** (काम का आखिरी दिन): The final day of one's employment.
 
 
• **Example:** Today is my** last day of work **before I retire.
